##### `deletion_policy`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="deletion_policy" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataLossPreventionContentPolicy.DataLossPreventionContentPolicy.Initializer.parameter.deletionPolicy"></a>

- *Type:* str

Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance.

Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/8.6.0/docs/resources/data_loss_prevention_content_policy#deletion_policy DataLossPreventionContentPolicy#deletion_policy}

##### `is_construct` <a name="is_construct" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataLossPreventionContentPolicy.DataLossPreventionContentPolicy.isConstruct"></a>

```python
from cdktn_provider_google import data_loss_prevention_content_policy

dataLossPreventionContentPolicy.DataLossPreventionContentPolicy.is_construct(
  x: typing.Any
)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataLossPreventionContentPolicy.DataLossPreventionContentPolicy.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* typing.Any

Any object.

##### `deletion_policy`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="deletion_policy" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataLossPreventionContentPolicy.DataLossPreventionContentPolicyConfig.property.deletionPolicy"></a>

```python
deletion_policy: str
```

- *Type:* str

Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance.

Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/8.6.0/docs/resources/data_loss_prevention_content_policy#deletion_policy DataLossPreventionContentPolicy#deletion_policy}

```python
)
```

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |

| <code><a href="#@cdktn/provider-google.dataLossPreventionContentPolicy.DataLossPreventionContentPolicyInspectConfigRuleSetRulesHotwordRuleLikelihoodAdjustment.property.relativeLikelihood">relative_likelihood</a></code> | <code>typing.Union[int, float]</code> | Increase or decrease the likelihood by the specified number of levels. |

---

##### `fixed_likelihood`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="fixed_likelihood" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataLossPreventionContentPolicy.DataLossPreventionContentPolicyInspectConfigRuleSetRulesHotwordRuleLikelihoodAdjustment.property.fixedLikelihood"></a>

```python
fixed_likelihood: str
```

- *Type:* str

Set the likelihood of a finding to a fixed value.

Either this or relative_likelihood can be set. Possible values: ["VERY_UNLIKELY", "UNLIKELY", "POSSIBLE", "LIKELY", "VERY_LIKELY"]

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/8.6.0/docs/resources/data_loss_prevention_content_policy#fixed_likelihood DataLossPreventionContentPolicy#fixed_likelihood}

---

##### `relative_likelihood`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="relative_likelihood" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataLossPreventionContentPolicy.DataLossPreventionContentPolicyInspectConfigRuleSetRulesHotwordRuleLikelihoodAdjustment.property.relativeLikelihood"></a>

```python
relative_likelihood: typing.Union[int, float]
```

- *Type:* typing.Union[int, float]

Increase or decrease the likelihood by the specified number of levels.

For example,
if a finding would be POSSIBLE without the detection rule and relativeLikelihood is 1,
then it is upgraded to LIKELY, while a value of -1 would downgrade it to UNLIKELY.
Likelihood may never drop below VERY_UNLIKELY or exceed VERY_LIKELY, so applying an
adjustment of 1 followed by an adjustment of -1 when base likelihood is VERY_LIKELY
will result in a final likelihood of LIKELY. Either this or fixed_likelihood can be set.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/8.6.0/docs/resources/data_loss_prevention_content_policy#relative_likelihood DataLossPreventionContentPolicy#relative_likelihood}

---

##### `put_likelihood_adjustment` <a name="put_likelihood_adjustment" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataLossPreventionContentPolicy.DataLossPreventionContentPolicyInspectConfigRuleSetRulesHotwordRuleOutputReference.putLikelihoodAdjustment"></a>

```python
def put_likelihood_adjustment(
  fixed_likelihood: str = None,
  relative_likelihood: typing.Union[int, float] = None
) -> None
```

###### `fixed_likelihood`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="fixed_likelihood" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataLossPreventionContentPolicy.DataLossPreventionContentPolicyInspectConfigRuleSetRulesHotwordRuleOutputReference.putLikelihoodAdjustment.parameter.fixedLikelihood"></a>

- *Type:* str

Set the likelihood of a finding to a fixed value.

Either this or relative_likelihood can be set. Possible values: ["VERY_UNLIKELY", "UNLIKELY", "POSSIBLE", "LIKELY", "VERY_LIKELY"]

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/8.6.0/docs/resources/data_loss_prevention_content_policy#fixed_likelihood DataLossPreventionContentPolicy#fixed_likelihood}

---

###### `relative_likelihood`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="relative_likelihood" id="@cdktn/provider-google.dataLossPreventionContentPolicy.DataLossPreventionContentPolicyInspectConfigRuleSetRulesHotwordRuleOutputReference.putLikelihoodAdjustment.parameter.relativeLikelihood"></a>

- *Type:* typing.Union[int, float]

Increase or decrease the likelihood by the specified number of levels.

For example,
if a finding would be POSSIBLE without the detection rule and relativeLikelihood is 1,
then it is upgraded to LIKELY, while a value of -1 would downgrade it to UNLIKELY.
Likelihood may never drop below VERY_UNLIKELY or exceed VERY_LIKELY, so applying an
adjustment of 1 followed by an adjustment of -1 when base likelihood is VERY_LIKELY
will result in a final likelihood of LIKELY. Either this or fixed_likelihood can be set.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/8.6.0/docs/resources/data_loss_prevention_content_policy#relative_likelihood DataLossPreventionContentPolicy#relative_likelihood}

---
